Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City vvww.dilg.gov.ph OILG OPINION NO OCT 14 2024 ATTY. EMKAY G. EVANGELISTA ATTY. GIANNA C. LALU Padiernos & Padiernos Law Offices Unit 2104 Antel Corporate Center 121 Valero St. Salcedo Village, Makati City Dear Attys. Evangelista and Lalu: This has reference to your letter seeking this Department's opinion regarding the passage of an Ordinance regulating the Public Utility Buses in the City of San Pedro, Laguna. Per your representation, on June 13, 2023, the Sangguniang Panlungsod of San Pedro, Laguna passed and approved Resolution 2023-125/City Ordinance Number 2023-16: An Ordinance Amending City Ordinance No. 2017-23, otherwise known as the "2017 Traffic Code of the City of San Pedro, Laguna. You mentioned that the said City Ordinance: 1. Prohibited Public Utility Buses (PUBs) to pass through the City of San Pedro portion of Manila South Road and other roads within the City of San Pedro unless otherwise as may be determined by the City Mayor; 2. Diverted the route of Public Utility Buses from Manila South Road and along arterial roads, highways, and identified collector roads within the territorial jurisdiction of San Pedro Laguna to other available and accessible routes such as the South Luzon Expressway and/or other routes as may be determined by the City Mayor; and 3. Gave the City Mayor wide latitude of choice and power to determine the other alternative routes for Public Utility Buses. Thus, the instant request for legal opinion on whether the Local Government Unit of San Pedro. through an ordinance. can prohibit the entry of Public Utility Buses into their territorial iurisdiction. At the outset, it is important to distinguish the terms "regulation" and "prohibition" in the context of an ordinance. Prohibition means outright prohibiting certain acts, or making a specific activity fully illegal and not authorized under any circumstances. While, "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

regulation does not forbid the activity outright but imposes specific conditions or standards that must be followed. In essence, prohibition eliminates the activity, while regulation controls and manages how the activity is carried out, ensuring it adheres to certain standards or conditions. Now, we answer the query in the neqative as we are of the considered view that the San Pedro City Ordinance No. 2023-16 is merely a regulatory measure. Such ordinance is anchored on Section 161 of the R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991. The Supreme Court, in the case of Mayor Magtajas V. Pryce Properties Corp.2, ruled that Ordinances anchored on Section 16 of the LGC or the general welfare clause should not be prohibitory and should not contravene a statute albeit they can provide for regulation. The rationale of the requirement that the ordinances should not contravene a statute is obvious. Municipal governments are only agents of the national government. Local councils exercise only delegated legislative powers conferred on them by Congress as the national lawmaking body. The delegate cannot be superior to the principal or exercise powers higher than those of the latter. It is a heresy to suggest that the local government units can undo the acts of Congress, from which they have derived their power in the first place, and negate by mere ordinance the mandate of the statute.3 Hence, the LGU of San Pedro may only regulate the entry of Public Utility Buses into their territorial jurisdiction as it is allowed by R.A. 4136, otherwise known as the Land Transportation and Traffic Code. Stated otherwise, what the national legislature expressly allows by law, such as regulation and use of local streets, a local government unit may not disallow by ordinance or resolution. Ours is still a unitary form of government, not a federal state. Being so, any form of autonomy granted to local governments will necessarily be limited and confined within the extent allowed by the central authority. Besides, the principle of local autonomy under the 1987 Constitution simply means "decentralization". It does not make local governments sovereign within the state or an "imperium in imperio"4 Thus, the LGU of San Pedro may only regulate the entry of Public Utility Buses within their territorial jurisdiction. However, we respectfully reiterate that statutes and ordinances are presumed valid unless and until the courts declare the contrary in clear and unequivocal terms. Considering that the San Pedro Ordinance No. 2023-16 has already been passed and approved, said ordinance enjoys presumption of validity. 1 Section 16. General Welfare. - Every local government unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local government units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants. 2 G.R. No. 111097 July 20, 1994 3 Ibid Hon. Lina Jr. V. Hon. Pano, G.R. No. 129093, August 30, 2001 Page 2 of 3

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: A VICTOR R. LLAMAS secretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/lasm Copy furnished ARIEL O.
